edges.effect_quant: The strongest pooled estimate comes from a 2022 meta-analysis of 3 randomized trials and 396 participants, where polaprezinc-based therapy improved intention-to-treat eradication with an odds ratio of 2.01 and per-protocol eradication with an odds ratio of 2.65 versus triple therapy alone.
edges.population: adults with Helicobacter pylori-associated gastritis or peptic-ulcer disease receiving zinc carnosine (polaprezinc) alongside triple therapy
edges.mechanism: Zinc carnosine may improve H. pylori eradication by stabilizing the gastric mucosal barrier, reducing oxidative injury, and creating a local environment that helps standard antibiotic therapy work more effectively.
edges.summary: The evidence supports zinc carnosine as an adjunct, not a stand-alone eradication therapy. When combined with standard triple therapy it tends to raise eradication rates modestly, which is useful in a space where antibiotic resistance steadily erodes margins.
edges.caveats: The evidence base is still small and comes mainly from East Asian trials using older triple-therapy backbones. Results may not translate perfectly to modern resistance patterns or to every eradication regimen.

evidence.notes: Efficacy and Safety of Polaprezinc-Based Therapy versus the Standard Triple Therapy for Helicobacter pylori Eradication: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.

evidence.notes: Polaprezinc, a mucosal protective agent, in combination with lansoprazole, amoxycillin and clarithromycin increases the cure rate of Helicobacter pylori infection.
